100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 24, 1926, the United States faced growing tensions as the Ford Motor Company continued to engage in labor disputes, sparking protests among workers demanding better wages and conditions. Across the Atlantic, the British Parliament discussed the ongoing crisis in Ireland, with hopes for a resolution amid rising sectarian violence. In entertainment news, the silent film "The General," starring Buster Keaton, premiered to critical acclaim, showcasing the enduring popularity of cinema in American culture.
